descriptionChirho: A protective body garment made of metal scales or links, worn in battle as defensive armor covering the torso. All four clusters denote the same physical object with different grammatical constructions: with article (eng: 'the breastplate / the armor', arb: الدِّرْعِ, kor: 그 갑옷, swa: dirii), bare or with article (eng: 'coat of mail', spa: 'coraza', arb: دِرْعًا, kor: 갑옷을, swa: deraya), with conjunction waw and plural (eng: 'and the armor', spa: 'y las corazas', arb: وَدُرُوعًا, kor: 그리고 갑옷들을, swa: na silaha za kuvaa), and with preposition kaf in simile (eng: 'like armor', spa: 'como coraza', arb: كَالدِّرْعِ, kor: 갑옷같이). Hindi कवच remains constant throughout.
